Reliability coefficients for a factor solution

Source: R/efa_reliability.R
efa_reliability.Rd

Computes model-based reliability coefficients for a factor solution: McDonald's omega (total, hierarchical, and subscale), standardized Cronbach's alpha, and the H index. For a solution with a general factor, it also computes the common-variance indices ECV and PUC. The result is a long-format table with one row per coefficient.

Usage

efa_reliability(
  model = NULL,
  coefficients = NULL,
  g_name = "g",
  group_names = NULL,
  factor_map = NULL,
  variance = c("correlation", "sums_load"),
  var_names = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  fac_names = NULL,
  g_load = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  s_load = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  u2 = NULL,
  cormat = NULL,
  pattern = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  Phi = NULL
)

Source

McDonald, R. P. (1985). Factor analysis and related methods. Hillsdale, NJ: Erlbaum.

McDonald, R. P. (1999). Test theory: A unified treatment. Mahwah, NJ: Erlbaum.

Cronbach, L. J. (1951). Coefficient alpha and the internal structure of tests. Psychometrika, 16, 297-334.

Zinbarg, R. E., Yovel, I., Revelle, W., & McDonald, R. P. (2006). Estimating generalizability to a latent variable common to all of a scale's indicators: A comparison of estimators for omega H. Applied Psychological Measurement, 30, 121-144.

Hancock, G. R., & Mueller, R. O. (2001). Rethinking construct reliability within latent variable systems. In R. Cudeck, S. du Toit, & D. Sörbom (Eds.), Structural equation modeling: Present and future - A Festschrift in honor of Karl Jöreskog (pp. 195-216). Lincolnwood, IL: Scientific Software International.

Arguments

model

An efa_fit(), efa_schmid_leiman(), psych::schmid(), or lavaan solution, or a loading matrix (see Input).

coefficients

character. A subset of the coefficients to return: any of "omega_total", "omega_hierarchical", "omega_subscale", "alpha", "H", "ECV", and "PUC". The default NULL returns all that the solution defines.

g_name

character. The name of the general factor of a lavaan bifactor or second-order fit. Default is "g".

group_names

character. Labels for the groups of a lavaan multiple-group fit, one per group.

factor_map

matrix. A logical or 0/1 matrix, variables by group factors, that assigns the variables to the group factors. A variable can belong to more than one factor. The columns must be in the column order of the solution. If NULL (default), see Input. Not used for lavaan input.

variance

character. The variance of each composite: "correlation" (default) takes it from the correlation matrix; "sums_load" uses the model-implied variance and needs no correlation matrix. Not used for lavaan input (see Details).

var_names, g_load, s_load, pattern

Give the loadings as one matrix in model instead.

fac_names

character. Labels for the group factors, in the column order of the loadings; for a single-factor solution, the label of its factor. Not used for lavaan input.

u2

numeric. Uniquenesses, one per variable, to replace the ones derived from a loading matrix in model.

cormat

matrix or data.frame. The correlation matrix of the variables, on the metric of the loadings, for variance = "correlation". Named variables are matched by name, else by position. If NULL, it is taken from the solution where available.

Phi

matrix. The factor intercorrelations of a pattern matrix in model. Not used for a fitted solution, and refused for the loading table of an efa_schmid_leiman() solution.

Value

An object of class efa_reliability: a data frame with one row per coefficient and the columns

coefficient

the coefficient name.

level

"general" for the general factor (or the factor of a single-factor solution), "total" for the whole scale of a correlated-factors solution, and "group" for a group factor.

factor

the factor label: "g" for the general factor, "total" for the whole scale of a correlated-factors solution.

group

the group of a lavaan multiple-group fit, else NA.

value

the coefficient value.

Coefficients that the solution does not define are omitted. The attributes are settings (the variance used, and whether the solution has no general factor), kind (reliability coefficient or common-variance index), and factor_map (the assignment of the variables to the group factors that was used: a logical matrix, a list of them for a multiple-group fit, or NULL for a single factor).

Details

Coefficients

Each row of the result describes one composite, that is, the unit-weighted sum of a set of variables: the whole scale, or the variables assigned to one group factor. Each omega is the share of the composite's variance that the model gives to the factors (McDonald, 1978, 1985, 1999; Zinbarg et al., 2005, 2006):

  • Omega total (omega_total): the share due to all factors. On a group-factor row, it is the omega S of Rodriguez et al. (2016a, 2016b).

  • Omega hierarchical (omega_hierarchical): the share due to the general factor. On the whole-scale row, it tells whether the total score measures one construct.

  • Omega subscale (omega_subscale): the share due to the group factors; on a group-factor row, the share due to its own group factor. There, it is the omega HS of Rodriguez et al. (2016a, 2016b): what the subscale score measures in addition to the general factor.

On the whole-scale row, omega total is omega hierarchical plus omega subscale. On a group-factor row, omega total can be larger, because cross-loadings on other group factors add true-score variance.

The other coefficients are:

  • Alpha (alpha): standardized Cronbach's alpha (Cronbach, 1951). It assumes essentially tau-equivalent variables and is a lower bound otherwise. For a multidimensional scale, it is rarely the coefficient to report (Gignac, 2014).

  • H index (H): the reliability of an optimally weighted composite (Hancock & Mueller, 2001). A low value shows that the variables do not define the factor well.

  • ECV and PUC (general factor only): the share of the common variance due to the general factor, and the proportion of correlations between variables of different group factors (Bonifay et al., 2015; Reise et al., 2013; Rodriguez et al., 2016a, 2016b). Together, they tell whether a unidimensional model is acceptable.

A solution without a general factor (a correlated-factors solution) gives omega total, alpha, and the H index of each factor, and omega total and alpha of the whole scale, whose row is labelled "total". Omega subscale is not given: it is the share in addition to a general factor, and when the factors correlate, it is not a share of the variance. A single-factor solution gives omega total, alpha, and the H index. Use semTools::compRelSEM() for composite reliability and semTools::AVE() for the average variance extracted of a lavaan fit.

Total variance

With variance = "correlation", the variance of a composite is the sum of its block of the correlation matrix, so residual correlations that the model does not reproduce change omega total. With "sums_load", it is the model-implied variance. lavaan input always uses the model-implied variance, which includes freed residual covariances. psych::omega() gives other values: it computes the whole-scale omega total from the residual variances, and it leaves cross-loadings out of the whole-scale omega subscale and of the omega total of a subscale.

Reverse-keyed and ordinal variables

The coefficients describe the raw sum of the variables as fitted. Variables keyed in the opposite direction decrease the true-score variance of that sum, and the function warns when it finds such variables. Reverse-code them before you fit the solution (Flora, 2020).

With polychoric or tetrachoric correlations, or a lavaan fit with ordered variables, the coefficients describe the sum of the latent continuous responses, not the sum of the ordinal answers. The two can be very different when the answers have few categories or are skewed. Green and Yang (2009) give an omega for the ordinal sum score; this function does not compute it.

Input

  • An efa_fit() solution. An oblique solution is a correlated-factors solution. An orthogonal solution is scored in the same way, with factor correlations of 0. A "bifactorT" solution is a bifactor solution, whose general factor is the factor that loads on every variable (the column whose smallest absolute loading is largest). A "bifactorQ" solution, whose group factors are correlated, and an unrotated solution with two or more factors are refused.

  • An efa_schmid_leiman() or psych::schmid() solution, or the loading table of an efa_schmid_leiman() solution: a bifactor solution.

  • A loading matrix. Without Phi, the first column is the general factor and the other columns are the group factors. With Phi, the matrix is the pattern matrix of a correlated-factors solution (not the structure matrix). Give the variable names as row names. A pattern matrix needs cormat for variance = "correlation".

  • A lavaan fit: single-factor, correlated-factors (cross-loadings are permitted), second-order, or bifactor. A fit is a bifactor solution if variables load on a factor named g_name and on other factors. Fit it with orthogonal = TRUE, because the coefficients need uncorrelated factors. A second-order solution is Schmid-Leiman transformed. A multiple-group fit is scored per group.

Without factor_map, each variable is assigned to the group factor with its largest absolute loading, and a variable without a group loading to none. A loading matrix or a Schmid-Leiman solution in which most variables have an exact zero group loading (a target matrix, or a transformed lavaan solution) uses its non-zero pattern instead. So does a lavaan fit, but in an ESEM block, each variable is assigned to the block's factor with its largest loading.

See also

efa_fit() for the solution these are computed from, and OMEGA(), the superseded function that returns these same coefficients in a wide, per-factor layout.

Other reliability coefficients: efa_schmid_leiman(), print.efa_reliability()

Examples

## From an oblique EFA (correlated-factors) solution. Each variable is assigned to the
## factor with its largest loading.
efa_mod <- efa_fit(test_models$baseline$cormat, N = 500, n_factors = 3,
                   estimator = "PAF", rotation = "promax")
efa_reliability(efa_mod)
#> 
#> ── Reliability coefficients ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#>         tot  alpha    H
#> total  .883   .868
#> F1     .769   .768  .760
#> F2     .765   .763  .753
#> F3     .745   .743  .738

## From a Schmid-Leiman solution, with an explicit variable-to-factor map.
sl_mod <- efa_schmid_leiman(efa_mod, estimator = "PAF")
fc <- sl_mod$sl[, c("F1", "F2", "F3")] >= .2
efa_reliability(sl_mod, factor_map = fc)
#> 
#> ── Reliability coefficients ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#>      tot  hier   sub  alpha    H
#> g   .883  .740  .143   .868  .842
#> F1  .769  .500  .269   .768  .463
#> F2  .765  .494  .270   .763  .472
#> F3  .745  .519  .225   .743  .408
#> 
#> ── Common-variance indices ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#>     ECV   PUC
#> g  .652  .706

## Request a subset of the coefficients only.
efa_reliability(sl_mod, factor_map = fc,
                coefficients = c("omega_total", "alpha"))
#> 
#> ── Reliability coefficients ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#>      tot  alpha
#> g   .883   .868
#> F1  .769   .768
#> F2  .765   .763
#> F3  .745   .743

## From an oblique pattern matrix and its factor intercorrelations. This is
## the same correlated-factors solution, and gives the same coefficients.
efa_reliability(efa_mod$rot_loadings, Phi = efa_mod$Phi,
                cormat = test_models$baseline$cormat)
#> 
#> ── Reliability coefficients ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#>         tot  alpha    H
#> total  .883   .868
#> F1     .769   .768  .760
#> F2     .765   .763  .753
#> F3     .745   .743  .738

## From lavaan fits: a bifactor solution, and a correlated-factors one.
# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("lavaan", quietly = TRUE)) {
mod_cf <- 'F1 =~ V1 + V2 + V3 + V4 + V5 + V6
           F2 =~ V7 + V8 + V9 + V10 + V11 + V12
           F3 =~ V13 + V14 + V15 + V16 + V17 + V18'
mod <- paste(mod_cf, 'g =~ V1 + V2 + V3 + V4 + V5 + V6 + V7 + V8 + V9 + V10 +
                           V11 + V12 + V13 + V14 + V15 + V16 + V17 + V18',
             sep = "\n")
fit <- lavaan::cfa(mod, sample.cov = test_models$baseline$cormat,
                   sample.nobs = 500, estimator = "ml", orthogonal = TRUE)
efa_reliability(fit, g_name = "g")

## No general factor: omega hierarchical, omega subscale, ECV, and PUC are omitted.
fit_cf <- lavaan::cfa(mod_cf, sample.cov = test_models$baseline$cormat,
                      sample.nobs = 500, estimator = "ml")
efa_reliability(fit_cf)
}
#> 
#> ── Reliability coefficients ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#>         tot  alpha    H
#> total  .882   .868
#> F1     .744   .743  .747
#> F2     .764   .763  .765
#> F3     .768   .768  .769
# }
